en: Itivuttaka 40 Dukanipāta, Second Chapter Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having thus spoken, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and went to his dwelling. Thereupon, the venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and said to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would explain to me in detail the meaning of this brief statement that the Blessed One spoke and then rose from his seat and went to his dwelling. "It is fitting for you, Ānanda, to think thus. Listen, Ānanda, and pay close attention; I will speak. "Yes, venerable sir," the venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One then said this: "Ānanda, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who is a doer of evil deeds and the person who is a doer of wholesome deeds. These, Ānanda, are the two kinds of persons found existing in the world. [The Blessed One then repeated the same teaching regarding the person who speaks ill and the person who speaks well, the person who is miserly and the person who is generous, the person who is of evil character and the person who is of good character. "These, Ānanda, are the two kinds of persons found existing in the world. When this was said, the venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, it is wonderful, it is marvelous! How well has the Blessed One explained the meaning of this brief statement! "It is fitting for you, Ānanda, to think thus. For it is by means of such a brief statement that I have taught the Dhamma in detail, and it is by means of such a brief statement that I have taught the Dhamma in detail. [The Blessed One then repeated the same teaching regarding the person who is a doer of evil deeds and the person who is a doer of wholesome deeds, etc. "These, Ānanda, are the two kinds of persons found existing in the world. Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having thus spoken, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and went to his dwelling. The Discourse on Clear Knowledge.
Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard:
"Bhikkhus, ignorance is the forerunner in the attainment of unwholesome states, followed by shamelessness and lack of moral dread."
“Monks, true knowledge (*vijjā*) is the forerunner of the attainment of wholesome states; conscience and shame follow after it.
Thus the Blessed One spoke. Regarding this, it is said:
“Whatever miserable destinies there may be,
in this world and in the next,
they all have ignorance as their root.”
They are the accumulation of desire and greed.
For one who is possessed of evil desires,
shameless, and disrespectful;
From that, one produces evil;
by means of that, one goes to a state of woe.
Therefore, [abandon] desire and greed.
By fading away from ignorance and arousing true knowledge,
a bhikkhu abandons all states of woe.
This matter too was spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The third [sutta].
